question: Why is the Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit marked out of date?
raw:
The permit is marked "out of date" in one audit only: the checklist audit of 12-auditor-checklist-deq-air.docx, run 2026-11-03. That audit read documents as of 2026-10-14.

**Why that line says out of date.** The checklist line asks for a current air permit that has not expired. The permit's own text reads "Expires: November 15, 2026." That is 12 days after the audit date. The audit uses "out of date" to mean the permit is close to expiring or needs follow-up. It does not mean the permit has expired. No reading gives an expiry date that has passed.

**Where the permit stands in your document list.** Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit No. 26-2841-ST-01 shows the state "Expiring," with an expiry of 2026-11-15. That is a separate label from the audit's word.

**What matters most: the renewal application.**
- The permit's Condition 1.3 sets the renewal application deadline at July 18, 2026. It reads: "no later than 120 days before the expiration date, that is, on or before July 18, 2026."
- The checklist audit (line A2) found nothing on file for the renewal application. The Oregon DEQ audit of the same date found nothing on file for the renewal application or a DEQ acknowledgment. Nothing on file means we have not been shown one. It does not mean it was not filed.
- Condition 1.2 says not to operate after expiry without a renewed permit or a timely renewal application. So whether a renewal was filed on time decides what happens on November 15.

**One fact I don't have:** was a renewal application sent to DEQ on or before July 18, 2026?
- If yes, the permit asks you to keep a copy and DEQ's receipt. Uploading both would bring these lines up to date.
- If no, contact DEQ right away, before November 15. The audit's own advice is to find out the status and next steps.

**What you didn't ask but should know.** Other air-permit lines are also open. They include the January–June 2026 semi-annual report, due July 31, 2026, and the March 14, 2026 carbon replacement record for C-1. All show nothing on file. The scrubber log also has gaps and an unexplained September 9 reading. Once you have the renewal paperwork, I can propose a fresh Oregon DEQ audit to update these lines.
